Prevention: Use clean planting materials with phytosanitary certificates to reduce spread of infestation into new fields.
Apply banding materials like grease or tangle foot to prevent ants from climping to the canopy to introduce the white flies.
Construct slippery bands of plastic sheets around the tree trunk at about one meter above the ground level.
In very infested areas, it is important to leave a period of 3 months rotating with grasses.
Avoiding sequential planting in the infected areas to avoid whitefly spread between fields.
Enhance natural predators of whiteflies (ladybirds, spiders, lacewing larvae and dragonflies) by planting
Monitoring: Inspect regularly for small white-winged insects with a yellowish- white abdomen and a light dusting of white powder (scales).
Check for ants climbing to the plant canopy to collect honeydew.
Inspect the infested parts for black sooty mold which may be sticky due to honeydew.
Consider to control when more than 60% of the sampled leaves have at least 10 flies per leaf.
Direct Control: Prune the highly infested plant parts and destroy by burning.
Collect fallen fruit and leaves and destroy by burning.
Spray the affected plant part with a mild solution of water with dish washing detergent at rate of 1 tea spoonful of detergent in 1L of water
Spray with biological control products like
Dudutech at 250 g per hectare with 1,500 – 2,000L of water every 5–7 days with 2–4 repeat applications.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Applaud 40SC at a rate of 30 mL /100L water).
